Gene Description

ATM is a large phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase-related protein serine/threonine kinase that coordinates cellular responses to DNA double-strand breaks. Recruitment and activation linked to the MRE11-RAD50-NBN complex enable phosphorylation of checkpoint and repair proteins, including p53, H2AX and CHEK2, helping coordinate cell-cycle arrest, DNA repair and damage-induced cell fate decisions. ATM also regulates telomere maintenance and responds to oxidative and nitrosative stress. Its predominant nuclear activity is complemented by regulated extranuclear pools, including ATM associated with the cytosolic surface of peroxisomal membranes during ROS signaling.

Core Functions

ATM is a PIKK-family protein kinase that executes MRN-linked DNA double-strand-break signaling through SQ/TQ substrate phosphorylation, coordinating checkpoints and DNA repair. Documented oxidative and extranuclear contexts use the same kinase, including a cytosol-facing peroxisomal membrane pool. Nuclear DNA-damage signaling is the dominant defining context. The peroxisomal membrane is a documented ROS-dependent context, not matrix residence or an integral-membrane prediction.

Molecular Function:
protein serine/threonine kinase activity
Directly Involved In:
DNA damage checkpoint signaling double-strand break repair
Cellular Locations:
nucleus peroxisomal membrane

Notes

(ATM-notes.md)

ATM manual review notes

ATM executes protein serine/threonine phosphorylation in nuclear DNA-damage signaling, coordinating checkpoints and repair. It also acts in telomere regulation and extranuclear stress responses. One molecular-function core is retained; the ROS-dependent peroxisomal membrane location is explicitly contextual. There is no NEW annotation or separate lipid, generic-binding or pexophagy core.

The reviewed map after Source65 closure retains all325 original source objects and the original null/absent alternative-products representation:214 ACCEPT,53 KEEP_AS_NON_CORE,44 UNDECIDED,12 MODIFY and2 REMOVE. The review enums govern the known-interaction versus unresolved-source distinction. Non-core association does not mean the reported pair is false; unread source-specific pairs remain uncertain. No new molecular activity is inferred from co-IP alone, no negative evidence is inferred from a paralog-focused title, and no PAINT assertion is rejected for a short donor list or target self-inclusion. Full ancestral tree/MSA placement was not replayed.

Assay chemistry and localization corrections

Rows197–208 replace matrix with peroxisomal membrane. In PMID:26344566(https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4589490/), selected Results and proteinase-protection Methods show accessible ATM alongside protected catalase. The correction retains association and cytosol-facing peripheral topology; it does not infer an integral membrane segment. Human fibroblast and human expression studies remain distinct from rat FAO and mouse fibroblast experiments. Cellular PEX5 phosphorylation/rescue and the in-vitro GST-p53 kinase Methods are not collapsed into purified ATM-to-PEX5 reconstitution. PEX ubiquitination, autophagy bridging and deubiquitination remain activities of the relevant other proteins. Exact nested Reactome physical-entity objects were not all replayed.

Rows246/262 remove the lipid-substrate activity and its explicit dependent GO0108 PI3P inference. The author-uploaded original PMID:11375976 Methods478–717, interaction Results775–826, kinase Results1241–1386 and Figure4D text1419–1442 were inspected independently. These are protein-substrate assays with kinase-dead controls. Wortmannin sensitivity is not evidence of phosphatidylinositol catalysis. The GO:0016303 reaction requires a lipid substrate. The complete PMID:8988033 abstract supplies a bounded negative lipid assay, not a universal absence proof. The normal11375976 cache is still abstract-only; its availability flag is unchanged by external reading. Only literal normal-cache text is quoted in the draft. No external Methods paragraph is fabricated into cached support.

The selected PMID:28508083(https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5425235/) Results/Fig1 text and kinase Methods establish purified human ATM activity on full-length human p53 and active dimeric preparations. Historical MRN/monomer pathway representations are not universalized. MRN-linked DSB signaling and radiation-responsive p53 phosphorylation are corroborated by complete normal abstracts15790808/9733515. ATM performs the signaling step; it is not assigned catalytic activities of its substrates, modifiers or downstream effectors.

Source closure and read limits

The normal seed and69 auxiliary-source imports are closed, with all preexisting records preserved. The provider attempt failed and generated no research report; its structured closure is retained without reading or reconstructing raw diagnostics. There was no duplicate gene-wide normal source request.

Source65 recovered one abstract-only publication and eight Reactome event records, now imported without overwriting existing files. All nine exact source bodies were read, and each official event location was checked. Thirteen source-dependent rows now retain supported kinase activity or nucleoplasmic location. The NEMO association remains non-core. At shortened telomeres, the KAT5 mechanism remains explicitly an inference from DNA-break biology. The other 311 rows, one core, 12 membrane replacements and two lipid-related removals are unchanged. No new process or molecular-function assertion was added.

The owner consultation read all68 available complete cached abstracts and102 complete Reactome summaries. The independent all325 peer read every proposed rationale/source tuple, rehashed all183 evidence pins and separately verified the highest-impact chemistry/topology/core evidence. It did not newly reread every one of those sources in full. Detailed source scopes are recorded per reference below and remain attributed to that consultation. Full cached availability does not imply full-body reading; exact pair tables, all figure pixels, supplements, nested event graphs and all donor experiments remain outside the stated scope.

id: Q13315
gene_symbol: ATM
product_type: PROTEIN
status: DRAFT
taxon:
  id: NCBITaxon:9606
  label: Homo sapiens
description: ATM is a large phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase-related protein serine/threonine kinase that
  coordinates cellular responses to DNA double-strand breaks. Recruitment and activation linked to the
  MRE11-RAD50-NBN complex enable phosphorylation of checkpoint and repair proteins, including p53, H2AX
  and CHEK2, helping coordinate cell-cycle arrest, DNA repair and damage-induced cell fate decisions.
  ATM also regulates telomere maintenance and responds to oxidative and nitrosative stress. Its predominant
  nuclear activity is complemented by regulated extranuclear pools, including ATM associated with the
  cytosolic surface of peroxisomal membranes during ROS signaling.

core_functions:
- description: ATM is a PIKK-family protein kinase that executes MRN-linked DNA double-strand-break signaling
    through SQ/TQ substrate phosphorylation, coordinating checkpoints and DNA repair. Documented oxidative
    and extranuclear contexts use the same kinase, including a cytosol-facing peroxisomal membrane pool.
    Nuclear DNA-damage signaling is the dominant defining context. The peroxisomal membrane is a documented
    ROS-dependent context, not matrix residence or an integral-membrane prediction.
  molecular_function:
    id: GO:0004674
    label: protein serine/threonine kinase activity
  directly_involved_in:
  - id: GO:0000077
    label: DNA damage checkpoint signaling
  - id: GO:0006302
    label: double-strand break repair
  locations:
  - id: GO:0005634
    label: nucleus
  - id: GO:0005778
    label: peroxisomal membrane
  supported_by:
  - reference_id: PMID:28508083
    full_text_unavailable: false
  - reference_id: PMID:15790808
    full_text_unavailable: true
  - reference_id: PMID:9733515
    full_text_unavailable: true
  - reference_id: PMID:26344566
    full_text_unavailable: false
suggested_questions:
- question: Which exact source experiments resolve the remaining ATM interaction pairs, constructs and
    genotypes, rather than only corroborating a known interaction elsewhere?
- question: Can the proteinase-accessible peroxisomal surface localization be reconciled with the current
    UniProt SL-0202 and Reactome matrix placements?
- question: What original evidence led to the lipid-kinase assignment from PMID:11375976, given its protein
    substrates and the dependent GO0108 PI3P inference?
- question: Which specialized donor or source assays support centrosome, spindle, synaptic-vesicle topology,
    meiotic and B-cell annotations that remain uncertain?
